spec.description: The observation stations the service knows about, optionally narrowed to a state or to named identifiers. Use it to find the station code `stations.get_observations` takes.

id.description: Station identifiers to return, such as `KSEA`. Sent as a repeated query key, one per identifier.

state.description: Two-letter state or marine-area codes to narrow to. Sent as a repeated query key.

cursor.description: Page cursor. The service does not hand this back on its own -- see the note -- so it is here for a caller who has one, not for a walk the client drives.

response.title: StationCollection
response.description: One page of stations, as a GeoJSON feature collection.

observationStations.description: The same stations as bare URLs, in the same order.

pagination.title: CollectionPagination
pagination.description: Where the next page is. A whole URL, not a bare cursor -- which is why this endpoint declares no pagination strategy.

next.description: URL of the next page, cursor already in the query string. Absent on the last page.

notes: No `pagination` block, deliberately. The service pages this endpoint, but it hands the next page back as a whole URL (`pagination.next`) rather than as the bare `cursor` value the request takes. Truewire's `token` strategy reads a cursor out of the response and sends it as a parameter; it has no way to say "take the `cursor` query parameter out of this URL". Declaring `cursor.from: "pagination.next"` would send the entire URL as the cursor and page nothing. So the walk is left undeclared rather than declared wrong.
